title: How Does Sharpness-Aware Minimization Minimize Sharpness?
main_claims: Full-batch SAM provably minimizes worst-direction sharpness (largest Hessian eigenvalue), not ascent-direction sharpness as naively implied by its formulation.
Stochastic SAM with batch size 1 minimizes average-direction sharpness (proportional to Hessian trace), which is the sharpness notion appearing in generalization bounds.
The key mechanism behind SAM's implicit bias is the alignment between the gradient and the top eigenvector of the Hessian, which emerges implicitly during training.
The two approximations in SAM's derivation individually lead to inaccurate local conclusions, but their combination accidentally recovers the correct effect for full-batch SAM.
methodology: The authors analyze SAM's implicit bias under a manifold-of-minimizers assumption (loss has a connected manifold of local minimizers with maximal-rank Hessian). They characterize the limiting ODE of full-batch SAM as Riemannian gradient flow with respect to the top Hessian eigenvalue, proving a two-phase dynamics: Phase I converges to the manifold, Phase II tracks sharpness minimization. Stochastic SAM with batch size 1 is analyzed under a separate setting. Both proofs rely on Taylor expansions for small perturbation radius rho and learning rate eta.
key_results: Theorem 4.5: Full-batch SAM tracks Riemannian gradient flow w.r.t. lambda_1(Hessian) on the loss manifold, with approximation error O(eta * log(1/rho)).
Theorem 5.4: Batch-size-1 SAM (1-SAM) minimizes average-direction sharpness (Hessian trace), not worst-direction sharpness.
The implicit Hessian-gradient alignment — gradient aligns with top eigenvector to within O(rho) — is the mechanistic driver of SAM's sharpness reduction.
Toy example confirms: full-batch SAM finds minimizer with smallest top eigenvalue, while GD on ascent-direction loss finds minimizer with smallest bottom eigenvalue.
limitations: Analysis requires small perturbation radius rho and learning rate eta; conclusions for large practical rho values are not formally guaranteed.
The manifold-of-minimizers assumption may not hold for all practical deep networks.
Mini-batch SAM (batch size between 1 and full batch) is not fully characterized — Hessian-gradient alignment does not necessarily hold in the general mini-batch case.
relevance_to_rq: Highly relevant to the RQ's sam_mechanism sub-topic: this paper provides the rigorous theoretical basis for what sharpness notion SAM actually minimizes (largest Hessian eigenvalue for full-batch; Hessian trace for stochastic), which is critical for interpreting sharpness measurements used in our empirical study comparing SAM and SWA.
